feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector leadership: clear positioning, relevant scope, and good evidence of progression and ownership. It reads professionally, but it is slightly repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond traffic/platform scale, and somewhat overstuffed with overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong headline and consistent progression from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Good credibility signals: recognizable organization, large-scale Drupal migration, analytics stack, studio buildout, and AI search project.  
- Writing is polished and generally error-free, with concise, action-led bullets and solid domain vocabulary.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than impact. Include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, revenue/support outcomes, or reduced publishing time.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma, and punctuation/hyphenation style varies slightly across sections. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several phrases already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language like “leading” or “driving” to sound more senior.
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent work, e.g. “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas and reducing the long list.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Drives enterprise website modernization, analytics and editorial infrastructure, and multimedia and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is close to the subtitle and competencies list.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize leadership-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Reframe as broader capability areas: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Cross-channel communications leadership
- Keep the most distinctive, senior-level differentiators: AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style for parallel structure; e.g., use “and” instead of mixing “&” with “and,” and prefer concise noun phrases
- Consider reducing from 8 to 6 items for sharper impact and easier scanning

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” are already strongly covered in the header and Topline Skills
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” also repeats detail already listed in Topline Skills and Technical + IT
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a repeat of the recent consulting and NACo experience rather than a distinct closing highlight. Tightening phrasing and making outcomes or scope more concrete would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, more specific verbs and trim filler: e.g., “Created AI-powered legislative search…” instead of “Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience…”
- Where possible, add scope or outcome signals: audience, platform, campaign purpose, or business value.
- Standardize style: use “AI-powered,” “10 x 20-foot,” and consistent serial commas.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with current freelance and NACo bullets.
- Anniversary campaign may add the most distinct value if framed as a standout cross-channel project rather than repeating general campaign language.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around strategic scope, technical ownership, and outcomes; add 1–2 concrete metrics if possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client scope: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper achievement-led lines, e.g.:
- “Built cross-functional digital workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search development, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and user-facing discovery experience.”
- Replace task phrasing like “deliver technical troubleshooting” with stronger ownership verbs: “implemented,” “optimized,” “resolved,” “modernized.”
- Add measurable outcomes where available: number of sites/pages supported, publishing teams enabled, campaign launches, performance gains, or search/discovery improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording repeats footer projects; keep this item at the role/responsibility level and let the footer hold named examples.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” also echoes NACo roles; emphasize what is new here: consulting scope, Drupal builds, and AI search.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more results-based: add growth, engagement, open/click rates, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten to one line.
- Tighten operations bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Video/studio language may duplicate the footer project section; focus here on organizational capability built, not recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth before the larger-scale platform/governance work in the next role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead line to focus on ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media, and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and specific: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very similar to the Director role; avoid repeating the same channel list.
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role unless this version stresses scaling/ownership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to recent leadership scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with tighter, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider adding one outcome-oriented qualifier if space allows, e.g. “for complex, multi-stakeholder organizations” or “at enterprise scale.”
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles like “audience-focused” beside broader capability labels.
- If you want stronger recency alignment, swap in “AI-enabled content discovery strategy” for “Audience-focused content planning,” reflecting current consulting work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to your current/most recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal, CMS modernization, and AI-enabled search first; they align best with the 2022–present roles.
- Remove lower-signal items if space is tight: keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if they are important for target roles.
- Use parallel structure and fewer nouns; avoid mixing platforms, coding languages, and outcomes in a long list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT.” Keep Topline Skills strategic; leave the fuller platform/tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Tightening it around decision-making and optimization impact will make it more senior and less repetitive.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g.:
  Analytics, Insights & Optimization: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI • KPI framework design • executive/leadership dashboards • SEO and web performance analysis • insight-driven optimization
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards” or “Executive reporting” for clearer, more standard phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure” or “decision-support reporting.”
- Keep only the most relevant platforms; if brevity matters, drop one of Looker Studio/Power BI unless both are important for target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may partially duplicate broader digital strategy language unless SEO is a target-role keyword.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming

- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo experience bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with more senior, specific language: “Broadcast video production,” “Livestream and webcast delivery,” “PTZ/multi-camera direction,” “Studio build-out and operations,” “Hybrid event production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia & live event production” already appears in Core Competencies; consider removing one or differentiating this section as execution-focused.
- “Studio operations” and event/video production are already evidenced in 2022–2024 and earlier NACo roles, so don’t overstate them here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since recent roles show strongest Drupal-led impact, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than breadth.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strength/relevance: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If formatting allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites)” to connect directly to recent impact.
- Keep this item platform-only and concise; move modernization or implementation language to adjacent technical items, where it’s already better supported.
- If space is tight, consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it has meaningful professional use; it reads less central than the others.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- Avoid repeating CMS modernization here; that theme is already covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more senior and implementation-focused by grouping tools by use and trimming lower-value/older terms.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle to emphasize application: “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Integrations.”
- Rewrite as grouped, cleaner skills: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API and tag integrations • Google Tag Manager • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • CI/CD and version control (GitHub Actions, Git/GitHub)”
- If accurate, replace “jQuery” with “JavaScript (ES6+)” and keep jQuery secondary, since it feels dated.
- Add only tools you’ve used recently in current/frequent work; if Cloudflare Workers or GitHub Actions were project-specific, consider moving them into project bullets instead.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Technical Execution” and “Technical Implementation” are semantically repetitive across sections.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and frame by function.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by purpose for faster scanning: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to recent work: Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project tracking)
- Keep only tools you’ve used recently or meaningfully; drop weaker/older platforms to emphasize current systems leadership

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them too prominently in multiple sections
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless collaboration tooling is central to the role; consider removing if space is tight

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Given the CV’s stronger emphasis on enterprise communications operations, this item should signal email/engagement capability more clearly and align with recent leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- If keeping it as a skills line, tighten to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add light functional context: **Email marketing, newsletter operations and audience engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- Put **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys** first, since it feels most enterprise-level and current; keep formatting consistent with other Technical + IT items.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience references to email/newsletter leadership; avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters” here unless you remove or shorten them elsewhere.
- “Engagement” may partially duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item platform-focused.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already evidenced in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize methods and decision-making value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics, Reporting & Optimization
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • dashboard development • SEO analysis • experimentation/A/B testing
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “dashboard development” or “executive reporting” for stronger phrasing.
- If accurate, consider adding one higher-value capability instead of another tool, e.g., “measurement strategy,” “conversion analysis,” or “performance reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is very close to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider merging or making one tools-only and the other outcomes-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating all of them elsewhere unless this section is strictly for ATS scanning.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” production volume, or team-building impact.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split the rest into 2 concise outcome-oriented bullets, e.g.:
- “Supported a major website refresh, contributing content, coordination and publishing improvements for NACo’s public-facing web presence.”
- “Produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow time saved.
- Remove “high-impact” unless you can prove it with results.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version framed as launching/early production, not scaling.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple roles; specify what changed or keep it lighter here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced multimedia and digital content assets to support program communications and research dissemination.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, stakeholders served, or audience/reach.
- Keep this entry lighter than later NACo roles since digital leadership is covered more strongly in 2015–2024 positions.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production” repeats across later roles; here, focus on podcast launch and innovation/research support instead.
- Avoid broad digital operations language that overlaps with Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets. Make it more tool-specific and concise so it complements, rather than repeats, your production experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Multimedia Tools
- Replace with: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want one workflow item, use: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast editing
- Keep “livestream studio workflows” out of this tools list and let it live under Topline Skills/work experience, where it already has stronger context and impact.
